transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Acme Health), Priya Menon (Dir Eng), Daniel Reyes (Head of Security), Maya Liu (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE for Redwood. With me is Samira, our solutions engineer. We're here to understand your reliability and incident tolerance needs and see if Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes the most sense.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Thanks. We appreciate it. Quick context - Acme Health is building patient-facing triage workflows, lots of PHI-ish content, need low latencies and very strict incident response.
[00:23] Priya Menon: We're evaluating latency SLOs at 200-300ms P95 for the majority of endpoints, and we do have spikes during evenings. Also compliance constraints — SOC 2 + regional data residency.
[00:36] Samira Khan: Got it. A few quick clarifying Qs - are you planning to start on Hosted and then move to Dedicated, or do you want Dedicated/Private from day one for compliance?
[00:45] Priya Menon: Ideally Dedicated or Private. We want predictability. But we wanted to understand Redwood's fallback and multi-region routing before we commit. If a region goes down, what's the behavior?
[00:56] Jordan Park: Good question. At a high level, we support policy driven routing: you can set region preference, failover regions, and capacity tiers. For Hosted customers we have automated fallback to secondary regions and model variants; for Dedicated we can pin capacity in two AZs or two regions depending on the contract.
[01:12] Daniel Reyes: When you say automated fallback, is that warm or cold? How long to redirect and spin up instances? For our SLA we need a predictable failover window.
[01:23] Samira Khan: Two layers to this. First, network-level routing — if a primary region is degraded, our front-door control plane will route to the next available region. Typical DNS/edge cutover plus internal routing usually happens within tens of seconds, but session affinity and ongoing generation requests might see some disruption. Second, model runtime warm pools: for Dedicated we maintain warm replicas and pre-loaded KV caches for pinned models, so tail latency during failover can be within the tens to low hundreds of ms for many workloads.
[01:48] Maya Liu: Tens to low hundreds sounds broad. Can you quantify in a pilot? We need numbers under real load, including cold starts when a model hasn't been used in 30 minutes.
[01:59] Samira Khan: Absolutely. We recommend a smoke benchmark during POC: your p95 under expected RPS and then an induced failover test to measure tail. We'll provide a benchmark harness and can run it on Dedicated or Hosted with similar model variants.
[02:12] Priya Menon: What about KV cache consistency? If we failover mid-session, do we lose context or do you have a copy in the failover region?
[02:22] Samira Khan: For session KV we do best-effort replication depending on config. For Dedicated and Private we can enable synchronous replication across two regions for KV cache or persist state externally via your storage. For Hosted the default is asynchronous cross-region replication to balance throughput and cost; there's a short window where some cache entries might not be there.
[02:41] Liam O'Connor: So for synchronous replication we need the Private or Dedicated option?
[02:45] Samira Khan: Correct — synchronous replication is generally available on Dedicated with multi-region pairs and on Private where you control networking, since it requires low-latency links and higher egress.
[02:55] Daniel Reyes: Encryption and key management during failover — how do you handle keys? We must ensure KMS/HSM keys remain in our control and accessible across regions.
[03:04] Jordan Park: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For Private deployments you can manage keys in-region. For Dedicated, we support customer-managed KMS with cross-region access patterns; we'll work with your security team to document the key rotation and access. We'll share the security guide.
[03:19] Daniel Reyes: Please include SAML SSO, RBAC details and audit log retention — those are deal-breakers.
[03:25] Jordan Park: Yep. We'll include SOC 2 artifacts, SAML metadata exchange steps, and audit log retention options. For Dedicated we offer longer retention windows as an add-on.
[03:34] Priya Menon: Back to SLAs — what's Redwood's priced SLA for Hosted vs Dedicated? And what's the incident classification + notification process?
[03:43] Jordan Park: Hosted: standard SLA is availability-based with a 99.9% target for API availability for paid tiers, but we recommend Dedicated for tighter guarantees. Dedicated can be contracted at 99.95% or custom SLOs depending on reserved capacity. Note that the SLA ties to control plane and runtime availability; regional outages that are outside our control have defined treatment in the contract.
[04:02] Priya Menon: And incident tolerance — do you have automatic model-variant fallbacks? Example: if GPT-like model variant A is overloaded or producing errors, will Redwood route to a lower-cost or quantized variant automatically?
[04:15] Samira Khan: We have model-variant fallback policies. You can configure ordered fallbacks (A -> A-quantized -> B-compat), plus automatic throttling. When a model returns specific error classes (OOM, kernel failure), the router can try a fallback variant. For mission-critical endpoints we suggest configuring strict validation, and in some cases we use dual-writing or fallback to a synchronous cache/result to avoid noisy outputs.
[04:39] Maya Liu: Dual-writing? Can you expand?
[04:41] Samira Khan: It's a pattern where critical prompts are sent to primary model and a cheaper/fast verification model; you use the verifier for quick sanity checks or failover. It increases cost but reduces user-visible failures.
[04:53] Liam O'Connor: How do you prevent a noisy fallback from silently changing outputs? We need guarantees for clinical prompts.
[04:59] Samira Khan: Good point. We recommend setting up a canary and validation pipeline: on fallback we tag results as fallback and route to a separate audit stream. You can enforce a hard block that rejects fallback outputs unless they pass a validator or human review. That is configurable per route.
[05:16] Priya Menon: Who owns the routing policy updates? Our security team wants the ability to lock fallback policies so product teams can't accidentally flip them.
[05:25] Jordan Park: RBAC integrates with the Console. You can restrict route/policy edits to specific roles. We'll show a demo of the policy UI in the next session.
[05:33] Daniel Reyes: What about multi-region consistency for rate limiting and quota enforcement? If we failover, do we risk double-charging or quota mismatch?
[05:43] Samira Khan: Quotas are enforced at a global control plane layer and are strongly consistent for Dedicated; for Hosted there is eventual consistency across edge caches which can create short windows of overage. We can enable stronger consistency at the cost of a small latency increase.
[05:58] Priya Menon: Sounds like Dedicated gives us the deterministic behavior we need, but cost is a worry. Can Redwood do hybrid: Hosted for dev and non-sensitive workloads, Dedicated for prod?
[06:09] Jordan Park: Yes, hybrid is common. Many customers start on Hosted for integration, then Dedicated for revenue-sensitive paths. We support routing by tag so traffic can be split by environment.
[06:18] Liam O'Connor: Can you walk through a typical post-mortem and RTO? If a region has a 5-minute outage, what's the expected RTO for our service?
[06:27] Samira Khan: RTO depends on configuration. With warm pools and synchronous replication, failover can be on the order of 30-90 seconds for new sessions, and sub-1s for cached requests. Cold starts increase RTO significantly. Our incident runbook includes automatic reroute + alerting + rollback to pinned model versions. We'll share the runbook but for contractual RTOs we align during Dedicated contract negotiations.
[06:49] Maya Liu: Can we get the runbook and sample playbook for tabletop exercises?
[06:53] Jordan Park: We'll attach the runbook. Samira will send the SRE playbook and a sample tabletop checklist.
[06:59] [Small crosstalk, someone drops for a sec]
[07:05] Priya Menon: On network egress — will cross-region replication increase our egress bill? We need clarity for cost modeling.
[07:12] Samira Khan: Yes, synchronous cross-region replication involves egress and potentially higher costs. We'll include an egress estimate in the worksheet. There are cost-optimized async options for Hosted.
[07:21] Daniel Reyes: Any support for private networking / VPC peering for Dedicated? We prefer no public internet in prod.
[07:27] Jordan Park: Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink; Private deployments are fully customer-controlled. We can run air-gapped packages for regulated customers.
[07:36] Liam O'Connor: How does rollback work if a model update causes a regression during a failover?
[07:42] Samira Khan: Console supports immediate rollback to pinned versions. We also have automatic canary rollouts and a health-check that will halt a rollout if error rates spike. During failover, we will not automatically switch model versions unless configured to do so; that's to avoid compounding issues.
[07:58] Priya Menon: Are there any customers in healthcare you can reference for reliability?
[08:03] Jordan Park: We can share redacted references and a short case study — will include in follow-up.
[08:09] Priya Menon: On telemetry: what granularity of traces and cost/latency breakdowns do you expose? We want token-level cost attribution per route.
[08:18] Samira Khan: We expose per-request tracing, token counts, per-model latency breakdowns and per-route cost attribution in Redwood Console. For Dedicated you can also export raw traces to your tracing system.
[08:29] Maya Liu: For our pilot, we want to test fallback under load and measure p95 and p99 before and after failover. Can Redwood script that?
[08:36] Samira Khan: Yes — our benchmark harness supports traffic shaping, induced region failover, and result validation. We'll run the test together during the POC.
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: Timeline check - we want a pilot in early Feb, then a production decision by mid-March. Is that feasible?
[08:52] Jordan Park: Feasible. We'll get the pricing worksheet and runbook to you this week, schedule a POC kickoff the week of Feb 3.
[08:59] Priya Menon: One more — how do you handle degraded model quality during noisy fallbacks? Does Redwood provide quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets?
[09:09] Samira Khan: Yes — Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts. During POC we can set up a baseline prompt set and alert if response quality or hallucination metrics degrade beyond thresholds.
[09:20] Daniel Reyes: For legal notices — in an incident that affects patient data, what's the notification SLA? We need timely notification for regulatory reporting.
[09:29] Jordan Park: Notification SLAs are part of the enterprise terms. We'll propose notification windows in the Dedicated contract and include escalation paths to our incident response team.
[09:38] Liam O'Connor: Any gotchas we should know about when moving from Hosted to Dedicated? Downtime during migration?
[09:44] Samira Khan: Migration is generally online — we replicate models and KV, warm up Dedicated instances, and cut traffic via routing policies. There can be short routing windows; we plan that with you.
[09:55] Priya Menon: If we need cross-region synchronous KV for safety, are there known performance impacts?
[10:00] Samira Khan: Synchronous replication adds RTT overhead; expect additional milliseconds per request depending on region distance. We can measure during POC and recommend placement.
[10:09] Liam O'Connor: Security question — can we get SOC2 plus penetration test reports?
[10:13] Jordan Park: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and a summary of pen tests; for Dedicated we can arrange attestation and additional audits as part of the enterprise package.
[10:21] Maya Liu: One operational question — during an AWS region outage, if Redwood's fallback routes to another cloud region, do you support cross-cloud failover?
[10:29] Samira Khan: We support multi-cloud and multi-region routing. We can route from AWS us-east to GCP region if configured, though that has complexity for KV consistency and egress. We'll include recommended patterns.
[10:41] Priya Menon: OK let's recap actions.
[10:44] Jordan Park: Recap: Jordan will send pricing/workbook and sample SLA; Samira will share the technical runbook, routing policy examples, and benchmark harness; Acme to confirm pilot SLOs and stakeholders. We'll schedule a follow-up to show the Console and policy UI and to kick off the POC.
[10:59] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good — thanks.
[11:02] Daniel Reyes: Thanks, please include contact for security lead.
[11:05] Jordan Park: Will do. Thanks everyone.
